query: Bed Six's Story Bed six is a second-year with Lake Fever, blue to the ears, who swears she never went near the lake. "I fell asleep in the bath," she says. From her chair, Sister Amaranth raises one eyebrow and keeps it there. The fever isn't breaking. A cure for a bath is not a cure for the lake. Get the true story out of her It comes out in a rush: the flat rock, a dare, four of them. The other three are in her dormitory, coughing into their scarves so nobody will know. You fetch them down one by one. By midnight the ward is full, and all four fevers are breaking. She sticks to the bath. You treat her for the lake anyway, on Sister Amaranth's say-so, and on Thursday three more second-years turn up blue to the ears. Treat what she tells you You dose her for a chill and get an early night. The fever takes three days longer than it should, and the chair across the ward watches every one of them.
